The second Spider-Man game developed by Insomniac and in my opinion, Is just as much a masterpiece as the first. A unique and interesting story following Miles Morales as well as a lot of combat changes that help Miles make himself distinct from Peter, but not from Spider-Man.

The swinging tricks and air maneuverability have also been improved with speed, mechanics, and animation fluidity as Miles swings through the city with finesse. There were fewer suits in this game compared to the first one, but I'd say the quality has improved as I've had more fav miles suits than I have Peter suits.

As the third Spider-Man entry arises next month, we turn towards even more Spidey content in the future, while not forgetting the two masterpieces that will lead up to it. Overall, a solid entry to the Marvel's Spider-Man series as well as an extraordinary stand-alone experience for fans of Miles and his personal rendition of Spider-Man.

It's pretty much to the first game what Arkham Origins was to Arkham City: not too radically different but with some new techniques for combat/stealth and a very compelling cast/story.

It's also not that long at all - whether it's a pro or con is up to you - I cleared it with some side stuff in about 15 hours with a 100% doable in a little over 20; comparing that to the first game's 50+ hours.

However, it's still a highly recommended successor. Especially if you're like me and just waiting a couple years for the sequel's PC release.

Spider-Man: Miles Morales shines not just as an action-packed superhero game, but as a heartfelt coming-of-age story. Set against a stunning wintery New York, the snowy streets add a fresh, atmospheric backdrop that makes every swing feel magical.

Playing as Miles is incredible—he’s not just filling Peter Parker’s shoes, he’s forging his own path. The story does a fantastic job of capturing Miles’ journey from a rookie trying to prove himself to a confident hero embracing his unique powers and responsibilities. His growth is genuine, relatable, and packed with emotion.

With electrifying combat and a vibrant world that feels alive, *Miles Morales* is more than a game—it’s an inspiring celebration of stepping up, standing out, and owning who you are. It’s a story that lingers like the first snowfall, quiet yet profound, leaving an imprint on your heart long after the final swing.

Fun game but was a little laggy in a few cutscenes. Nothing a slight change is graphics can't fix. I got it half off which I believe is the better option if you are to buy it. I had fun with two playthroughs on but it lacks end-game content.

An Amazing Winter Web-Slinging Experience (If you can catch it on sale!)

Miles was set up perfectly in Spider-Man Remastered, and this game does a fantastic job expanding on his character and diving deeper into his past. Setting the game in wintertime Harlem was an incredible choice—it gives the city a completely different, refreshing vibe compared to the first game. The Christmas lights and winter ambiance look amazing. Honestly, I almost wish I had played this during the winter instead of the summer just to match the atmosphere! As for the villains, the game handles them great. Without giving too much away, I'll just say it really is a small world!

While Peter definitely has the edge when it comes to the sheer number of gadgets, Miles' unique abilities are awesome. The addition of Venom blasts and camouflage completely changes the combat flow, allowing you to play much more aggressively than you could with Peter. It makes stepping into Miles' shoes feel fresh and distinct, making the expansion entirely worthwhile.

The PC port is fantastic. The game ran smoothly for me with zero lag, even on the highest settings. The winter environments really shine and perform flawlessly.

If you're a fan of Spider-Man games or the character in general, I highly recommend this. However, the main storyline is noticeably shorter than Spiderman Remastered. Because of the shorter runtime, I definitely recommend picking this up when it goes on sale.

Story: 8/10 ~ I'd say this game is a good 60% of what the first game was. Personally, I think the side activities and swinging made up for it.
Combat: 8/10 ~ Less gadget options but you do have his Venom power which allows for more options. The enemies you deal with this game are a lot more annoying than the ones in the previous game though. Active Camo makes stealth a cakewalk.
Overall: 4/5 ~ In terms of bringing Miles into the story line and fully transitioning the first game into the upcoming second one, this game did that exceptionally well. I also prefer the swinging in this game rather than the first one, same as the stealth situations, but I find myself preferring the combat of the first one with Peter's gadgets and suit abilities.
